newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-POLICE PASS SCHMEICHEL-WRIGHT RACE REPORT TO CPS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POLICE PASS SCHMEICHEL-WRIGHT RACE REPORT TO CPS.

text.p: Police have passed a report into allegations that Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel racially abused Arsenal's black striker Ian Wright to the Crown Prosecution Service.

The English Football Association (F.A.) confirmed the report was with the CPS late on Thursday, 24 hours after animosity between the two players dating back to November resurfaced in a match at Highbury.
The police investigation followed allegations from television viewers that Schmeichel verbally abused Wright during a league clash at United's Old Trafford ground on November 16.
If the CPS decides the evidence is strong enough, Schmeichel will become the first soccer player in Britain to face criminal charges for alleged racist abuse.

The escalating dispute between the volatile Schmeichel and Wright, whose disciplinary record is as bad as his scoring record is good, is threatening to overshadow all future clashes between the two premier league sides.
Wright was fortunate not to be sent off after a two-footed challenge on Schmeichel on Wednesday which left the United goalkeeper writhing in agony on the edge of his penalty area.

Wright, who had been booked before the incident, claimed the Dane was play-acting. As the players left the pitch at the end of the match he had to be restrained by stewards as he tried to confront Schmeichel.
Police intervened to keep the two players apart.
United manager Alex Ferguson leapt off the bench at the time of the original challenge but refused to comment on it after the match, which United won 2-1.
However, Ferguson said on Sky Sports television on Friday: "We are very surprised that this wild card has emerged about a racist remark allegedly made to Ian Wright.
"We can categorically deny that there has been any racist remark whatsoever from Peter Schmeichel. There's no question of that. It is very, very disappointing to read that stuff."
Ferguson said Schmeichel was very upset about the accusations.
"His own family back in Denmark are reading all this and it's very, very upsetting to the boy."

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger said: "Every time Ian Wright is involved in anything it becomes a major issue with the whole country talking about it. I don't know if anything happened in the tunnel, I can't speak about that."
Wright was quoted in British newspapers on Friday as saying Schmeichel made another racist remark on the way to the tunnel.

"It was racial and completely out of order," the striker was quoted as saying in the tabloid Daily Mirror. "You could see from my reaction how incensed I was. I wouldn't get like that if it was an ordinary insult."
The F.A. confirmed on Friday they had received a match report from referee Martin Bodenham but had yet to decide what action, if any, to take against the two players.
Wright's booking on Wednesday night means he will be banned for two matches from March 5 regardless of any further F.A. action.
